name: Estimate weights by feel
blurb: Useful for cooking, luggage and shopping. It works by building a mental library of reference weights and comparing against them.
gear: A kitchen scale and a luggage scale
steps: Build reference points: hold a 1 kg bag of sugar, a 5 kg weight and a 10 kg one until each is familiar.
Practise in the kitchen: guess the weight of every ingredient before it goes on the scale.
Learn density cues — the same size in metal, wood and plastic weighs wildly differently, and volume alone will mislead you.
Practise with luggage, which is the highest-stakes everyday use, then check on a luggage scale.
Learn to estimate by lifting in a consistent way: same hand, same posture, brief hold.
Log guesses and actuals for a fortnight and watch the error shrink.
tips: Awkward shapes feel heavier than compact ones of the same mass. Correct for it.
Recalibrate periodically. Your reference sense drifts.
proof: Ten items estimated within 15% of actual weight, across a range of sizes.
